correctness.rationale: For odd regular polygons the edge middle sets are computed exactly as segments joining longest-diagonal midpoints. Their hull is a smaller regular polygon, so its vertices are convexity points by Schneider. Conversely, any convexity point must lie on the middle hedgehog by the exact middle-line criterion. At a noncorner middle-set point the middle-line equation has a strict local extremum, whereas anti-periodicity forces a sign-changing zero within a half-turn; this contradicts the criterion. The proof is universal in odd n and does not rely on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The primary literature juxtaposes examples with exactly three convexity points against a theorem that typical bodies have infinitely many. The result fills a natural explicit gap by giving, in the canonical regular-polygon family, every odd finite cardinality n>=3 together with the complete point set and an exact radius. The longest-diagonal description is structural and directly tied to the middle-hedgehog machinery, not an arbitrary parameter computation.
